title: A River That Moves Its Own Banks
title_ja: 自ら川岸を変えていく川
fact_notes: 登場人物・活動・場所・観察結果は架空の教育事例。特定の実在の調査・製品・制度を報告するものではない。参考リンクは制作台帳であり外部の実証資料ではない。

sentences.en: On a field trip to a protected river valley, a class compared two drawings of the same stretch of river made many years apart.
sentences.ja: 保護された河谷への校外学習で、クラスは何年も離れて描かれた同じ河川区間の二枚の図を比較した。

sentences.en: In the older drawing, the river ran close to the eastern edge of a wide meadow, whereas the newer drawing showed a different curve.
sentences.ja: 古い図では川が広い草地の東端近くを流れ、新しい図では異なる曲線が描かれていた。

sentences.en: Some students assumed that workers must have deliberately changed the route of the river during a construction project.
sentences.ja: 生徒の一部は工事中に作業員が意図的に川の経路を変えたに違いないと思った。

sentences.en: Their guide explained that a river can gradually change the shape of its channel through the movement of water and sediment.
sentences.ja: 案内係は、川は水と土砂の移動によって徐々に流路の形を変えることがあると説明した。

sentences.en: The students examined a bend in the river from a safe observation point and described the features they could see.
sentences.ja: 生徒たちは安全な観察地点から川の曲がりを調べ、見える特徴を記述した。

sentences.en: On one bank, they saw exposed soil and the roots of plants extending outward from the edge of the land.
sentences.ja: 一方の岸ではむき出しの土と、陸地の縁から突き出た植物の根が見えた。

sentences.en: On the opposite side of the bend, a shallow area appeared to contain recently deposited sand and small stones.
sentences.ja: 曲がりの反対側では、浅い場所に最近堆積したと思われる砂や小石が見えた。

sentences.en: The guide reminded them that these observations alone could not establish exactly how quickly either bank was changing.
sentences.ja: 案内係はその観察だけではどちらの岸がどの程度の速さで変化しているかを正確に確定できないと念を押した。

sentences.en: Back at school, the students used an artificial channel to explore how flowing water might move different kinds of material.
sentences.ja: 学校に戻ると、生徒たちは人工の水路を使い、流れる水が異なる種類の物質をどう動かすか調べた。

sentences.en: They observed the movement of grains of sand and recorded where the material accumulated after the water had passed.
sentences.ja: 砂粒の移動を観察し、水が通過した後に物質がどこにたまったか記録した。

sentences.en: Although the model allowed them to observe changes within a short period, it did not reproduce the complexity of the actual valley.
sentences.ja: モデルでは短時間で変化を観察できたが、実際の谷の複雑さを再現したわけではなかった。

sentences.en: The class therefore treated the activity as an illustration of a possible process rather than a complete explanation of the historical drawings.
sentences.ja: そこで活動を歴史的な図面の完全な説明ではなく、起こり得る過程の例として扱った。

sentences.en: The project also raised questions about how nearby communities should respond when the boundaries of a river begin to shift.
sentences.ja: 活動は、川の境界が移動し始めると近隣地域がどう対応すべきかという疑問も生み出した。

sentences.en: Protecting buildings and roads may require measures that differ from those appropriate for an undeveloped stretch of the river.
sentences.ja: 建物や道路を守るには、未開発の河川区間に適したものとは異なる対策が必要になる場合がある。

sentences.en: The students discussed why a strategy that worked in one location might have undesirable consequences if applied everywhere.
sentences.ja: 一か所で有効な方策が、あらゆる場所に適用されると望ましくない結果を招く可能性を議論した。

sentences.en: They concluded that any practical recommendation would require more information about local conditions than they had collected during one visit.
sentences.ja: 実用的な提案には一回の訪問で集めた以上の現地条件の情報が必要だと結論づけた。

sentences.en: The two drawings had encouraged the students to see the river as a changing system rather than a fixed line on a map.
sentences.ja: 二枚の図によって、生徒たちは川を地図上の固定された線でなく変化する仕組みとして見るようになった。

sentences.en: They began to distinguish evidence of change from evidence explaining the causes and speed of that change.
sentences.ja: 変化の証拠と、変化の原因や速度を説明する証拠を区別するようになった。

sentences.en: Understanding natural processes, they discovered, sometimes requires observing the same place repeatedly over an extended period.
sentences.ja: 自然の過程を理解するには同じ場所を長期間繰り返し観察する必要がある場合があると分かった。

sentences.en: A landscape that appears stable during a single afternoon may be undergoing changes that become visible only with time.
sentences.ja: 一日の午後には安定して見える景観でも、時間とともに初めて見える変化が進んでいるかもしれない。

questions.prompt: What difference appeared in the two drawings?
options: The valley had disappeared completely.
The river followed different curves.
The pictures showed two unrelated rivers.
The students had drawn one picture that morning.
questions.explanation_ja: 同じ川で曲がり方が異なっていた。

questions.prompt: What did some students initially assume?
options: People had deliberately changed the river during construction.
All rivers remain in the same place.
The earlier drawing was a weather forecast.
Workers had filled the entire valley.
questions.explanation_ja: 工事が経路を変えたと思った。

questions.prompt: What did the students see on one bank?
options: A new school building.
A concrete bridge under construction.
Exposed soil and plant roots.
Large numbers of boats.
questions.explanation_ja: むき出しの土と根を観察した。

questions.prompt: Why could the students not determine the speed of change?
options: The river contained no sediment.
The guide had measured the speed already.
The students had been given all historical records.
One observation did not reveal how quickly the banks were changing.
questions.explanation_ja: 一回の観察だけでは変化速度を確定できない。

questions.prompt: What did the classroom model help them observe?
options: The movement and accumulation of material.
Every condition in the river valley.
The exact age of each historical drawing.
The location of all buildings in the town.

questions.prompt: Why did the class treat the model as an illustration?
options: It reproduced every aspect of the valley precisely.
They had not used water in the model.
They believed models could never provide information.
It simplified the real environment and did not explain every historical detail.
questions.explanation_ja: 実際の環境を単純化した例であり完全な説明ではない。

questions.prompt: What did the students discuss about protecting nearby areas?
options: All river areas should be managed in exactly the same way.
Different conditions may require different measures.
Every building must eventually be removed.
A single visit would settle every question.
questions.explanation_ja: 条件ごとに対策が異なり得る。

options: Difficult to see.
Recently discovered.
Unwanted or unfavorable.
Extremely predictable.
questions.explanation_ja: 望ましくないという意味。

questions.prompt: What distinguishes evidence of change from evidence explaining change?
options: The former shows that change occurred; the latter addresses how or why it occurred.
Both necessarily reveal the exact same facts.
Only the former can be collected over time.
The latter proves that every river is stable.
questions.explanation_ja: 変化の存在と、その原因・速度の証拠は別。

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Every change in a river is caused by construction.
Understanding a changing river requires observation, careful interpretation, and attention to local conditions.
Models can fully explain natural systems without field observations.
Rivers should always remain in their original channels.
questions.explanation_ja: 反復観察と慎重な解釈、地域の条件が重要。

grammar.focus: whereas the newer drawing showed a different curve
grammar.explanation_ja: whereasは二つの図の違いを対比。

grammar.focus: could not establish exactly how quickly
grammar.explanation_ja: 間接疑問how quicklyがestablishの内容を示す。

grammar.focus: Although the model allowed them to observe
grammar.explanation_ja: althoughは譲歩、allow＋人＋to不定詞は人が〜できるようにする。
may＋進行形は進行中の可能性を示す。

discourse.role_ja: 古い図と新しい図の対比。
モデルで可能なことと限界を示す。
モデルの限界から慎重な扱いへ。
自然観察に加えて社会的な課題を導入。

paraphrases.source: In the older drawing, the river ran close to the eastern edge of a wide meadow, whereas the newer drawing showed a different curve.

paraphrases.explanation_ja: 古い図と新しい図では川の形が違う。

paraphrases.source: The guide reminded them that these observations alone could not establish exactly how quickly either bank was changing.
paraphrases.rewrite: The guide said that one set of observations could not determine the precise rate of change on either bank.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 一度の観察で速度は分からない。

paraphrases.source: Although the model allowed them to observe changes within a short period, it did not reproduce the complexity of the actual valley.
paraphrases.rewrite: The model made it possible to notice changes quickly, yet it could not recreate all the conditions of the real valley.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 短時間の観察は可能でも現実を完全再現しない。

paraphrases.source: A landscape that appears stable during a single afternoon may be undergoing changes that become visible only with time.
paraphrases.rewrite: A place that seems unchanged over an afternoon might actually be changing in ways that take time to notice.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 安定して見えても時間をかけて分かる変化があり得る。
